newsitem.title: CANADA: Eurocan close to Zaire mine deal.
newsitem.headline: Eurocan close to Zaire mine deal.

text.p: Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd said on Friday it was close to finalizing a deal with the government of Zaire giving the company rights to the huge Tenke Fungurume copper-cobalt deposit in Zaire.

Eurocan finalized all the necessary arrangements to set up a joint venture with Zaire's state-owned mining company, Gecamines, and was just awaiting a signing ceremony, Eurocan spokeswoman Sophia Shane said.
"There's certainly some happy anticipation of the deal being completely wrapped up," she said in a telephone interview.
She said the signing ceremony was expected today or early next week.
The company said it was optimistic the agreement would be formally completed by November 30.
Eurocan would gain a 55 percent interest in Tenke Fungurume in exchange for US$250 million and a commitment to develop the property, Shane said.
Once the deal was completed, Eurocan chairman Adolf Lundin would be issued 30 million shares of Eurocan, she said.
The deal had no connection to Lundin's International Petroleum Corp, she said.
International Petroleum is based in Vancouver.

Tenke Fungurume, in Zaire's Shaba province near Zambia, holds at least 222 million tonnes of resource grading 4.42 percent copper and 0.33 percent cobalt, according to estimates done before Eurocan began looking at the property, Shane said.

"But we anticipate it will be several times that," she added. A consortium led by Cornucopia Resources, which included metals giants Inco Ltd and Phelps Dodge, also bid on Tenke Fungurume through Zaire's president, while Eurocan worked through the prime minister.
With this week's arrangements between Eurocan, Gecamines and the Zaire government, "Cornucopia will be out of the picture," said Shane.
Tenke Fungurume was previously explored by a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, which invested almost US$300 million in the project but walked away because of political risk.
Lundin is Swedish, but the mining agreement had no Swedish connection, Shane said.
